observations.composition: A curled orange-gold campfire and crossed split logs occupy the lower-left foreground. One large faceted firefly hovers in the upper-right, facing left toward the fire, with almost no overlap between the two masses.
observations.eyesAndPerspective: The near eye is clearly visible on the head. The far eye appears as a narrow dark sliver at the far edge of the face. The head points left toward the fire; the thorax follows to the right and the luminous-colored abdomen slopes down-right.
observations.drawingAndMaterial: Connected bronze, copper, and gold facets cover the insect and pale wings. Curving flame tongues have continuous warm shading and sculptural volume. Split wood has grain, dark charred edges, visible end planes, and ember seams.
observations.interestPoint: The separate campfire anchors the composition and gives the approaching firefly an external object of attention.
observations.matteAndEffects: The backdrop is near-white rather than uniform pure white. No obvious external flame bloom is visible, but the logs cast a soft contact shadow onto the matte.
caveats: The insect remains visually large relative to the fire and wood.
The far eye is only a narrow sliver, requiring owner review after the prior missing-eye and perspective feedback.
The abdomen trails down-right rather than the planned upper-right direction.
Very little overlap makes the requested depth ordering less explicit.
The top and right wing tips have narrow canvas margins.
The near-white field and baked-in log contact shadow need a dedicated matte assessment after approval.
